articleTitle: Evaluating Quality of Service: Throughput, Packet Loss, and Delay in Tree Topology with Ryu and Pox Controllers in Software-Defined Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Software Defined Network (SDN) marks a significant shift from conventional networking by decoupling the control plane from the data plane within the network infrastructure. This decoupling requires a protocol to facilitate communication between these two planes. OpenFlow, being open source, offers multiple controller options, making the choice of an appropriate controller pivotal for achieving optimal network performance. This research examines the Quality of Service (QoS) in a tree topology by comparing two distinct controllers, Ryu and Pox, within an SDN setup utilizing the Mininet emulator. The study involves implementing and testing both controllers to assess network performance based on QoS parameters including throughput, packet loss, and delay. Data collection and analysis were conducted using the Wireshark tool, with the Tiphon standard serving as the benchmark for determining indices and categories. The findings reveal that the Pox controller achieves higher throughput compared to the Ryu controller, whereas Ryu demonstrates superior performance concerning delay. The packet loss metrics were found to be relatively similar between the two controllers. This research offers insights for selecting controllers to enhance network performance in SDN environments by considering essential QoS parameters.

articleTitle: A novel mathematical model for optimizing energy consumption in OLSRv2 routing protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Device-to-Device (D2D) communication system is one of the fundamental elements of Fifth generation (5G) and Beyond 5G (B5G) mobile telecommunication networks. The fundamental architecture necessary for the implementation of efficient D2D communication system are the routing protocols. The initial version of routing protocol called Optimised Link State Routing Protocol (OLSR) v1 faced many challenges such as minimising energy. However, the introduction of OLSRv2 as a successor of OLSRv1 brings flexible techniques for message exchange among nodes and efficient signaling. However, the OLSRv2 routing protocol raises several difficulties, including those related to energy consumption. In this paper we therefore introduced a new model that computes the energy consumption in a static scenario in the OLSRv2 routing protocol considering various nodes. The simulation results for the energy consumption in the static scenario using our new model for $10,30,50$ and 100 nodes are obtained and compared with the energy consumption in the OLSRv2. The results show that the new model significantly outperforms OLSRv1 and OLSRv2 in terms of minimising energy consumption. The results are validated by computing the energy consumption in the static scenario using some default current values and the results show that the energy consumption is minismised compared to the OLSRv2. The energy consumption with various mobility speeds and routing overhead for both static and with various mobility speeds will be considered in our future paper.

articleTitle: Wastewater Aeration process based Cloud-SCADA/PLC System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: To protect public health and the environment, it is important to have effective wastewater treatment methods. Traditional methods of wastewater treatment plants require manual operation or SCADA systems are typically installed on site to control aeration during wastewater treatment. These traditional practices lack scalability and capabilities for remote monitoring and real-time optimization. This article discusses how modern cloud-based SCADA/PLC systems through Node Red software and totally integrate portal software (TIA) can transform wastewater aeration operations. Cloud-SCADA/PLC systems use the power of cloud computing to provide industrial automation with a powerful and flexible platform. Real-time data is collected from sensors placed at points such as treatment processes, dissolved oxygen (DO) levels and other aeration processes using programmable logic controllers (PLCs) located in the plant itself. This information is sent securely to a cloud-based SCADA system that allows for central monitoring control as well as data analysis via the control centers that have been designed.

articleTitle: Enhanced Flood Detection on Highways: A Comparative Study of MobileNet and VGG16 CNN Models Based on CCTV Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Flooding is one of the most common natural disasters, especially during the rainy season. Flooding on highways can cause material losses and casualties, as well as disrupt community mobility and adversely affect the economic sector. Early flood detection can help reduce the impact of these natural disasters. This research was designed to detect the occurrence of flooding on highways by comparing the performance of two Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures, namely MobileNet and VGG16, for the detection and classification of flood images on highways. This research used a dataset consisting of 2,000 images, with 1,000 images for the flood class and 1,000 images for the non-flood class. The results showed that the MobileNet model performed better than the VGG16 model. The MobileNet model has an accuracy of 99% and a shorter computation time, which is only 9 seconds, while the VGG16 model has an accuracy of 96% and takes 69 seconds for computation time. Based on the results of this study, it can be concluded that the MobileNet model can be used for early detection of flooding on highways. It is proven to have high accuracy and a shorter computation time; therefore, it can be used in real-time flood detection systems.

articleTitle: Predicting the Severity of Parkinson’s Disease Based on Voice Analysis Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder characterized by motor and non-motor symptoms. Prompt and precise identification of the severity of Parkinson’s disease is crucial for customized treatment strategies and enhanced patient care. This study utilized voice data and deployed several convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), autoencoder, and 1D CNN, to accurately predict the severity of Parkinson’s disease (PD). This analysis utilizes a dataset of speech recordings from patients with Parkinson’s disease at different levels. These severity levels are utilized to reflect the degree of Parkinson’s disease severity in the study. The voices have undergone preprocessing, and a feature extraction method has been performed to enhance the voice features, specifically focusing on phonation, articulation, and prosody. Correlation-based feature selection is used to decrease the number of dimensions. The CNN models are trained to extract pertinent elements from the audio data, allowing for the categorization of PD severity. The experimental results indicate that the LSTM, autoencoder, and 1D CNN models achieved accuracy rates of 98%,95%, and 96% respectively, which are highly promising.

articleTitle: Integrating Blockchain With IoT-Edge-Cloud Netwotk for Tracking Offloaded Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Edge and cloud computing offer cost-effective computational options, including free services, for IoT devices with limited resources. Offloading refers to the practice of transferring tasks to the edge and/or cloud systems. Meanwhile, blockchain technology is increasingly used in various applications for its ability to decentralize decision-making and ensure data integrity and traceability in a transparent manner, eliminating the need for intermediaries. However, integrating edge and cloud computing with blockchain presents challenges. Blockchain integration can increase processing times, add complexity, and require additional storage for the blocks it generates. This paper proposes a network that combines edge and cloud servers to handle task offloading with different execution times from various devices, such as IoT, mobile, and other computing devices. To ensure the integrity of these offloaded tasks, the network incorporates blockchain technology, using a simplified, voting-based consensus algorithm for block validation. The theoretical framework is based on queueing models, particularly those with general service time distribution and single or multiple server setups. Experimental results, drawn from tests with both local and remote clouds, indicate that integrating blockchain only slightly affects overall response times. However, implementing blockchain requires additional storage, which poses a challenge for devices with limited resources.

articleTitle: A Combination Model Of Utaut, Hot, And Contextual Variables For Analyzing Farmers’ Behavior Towards Internet Of Things (IoT)-Based Agricultural Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Agriculture is a significant contributor to Indonesia’s economy, but its productivity falls short of expectations due to various problems, including insufficient human resources and dependence on manual land management methods. The implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) technology in the agriculture industry holds the potential to enhance production and effectiveness, however its adoption remains limited. Furthermore, climate change intensifies the difficulties encountered by farmers, necessitating inventive remedies. This study seeks to examine the determinants that impact farmers’ compliance with IoT-based agricultural technology, employing the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), Human, Organization, and Technology Fit (HOT FIT), and Contextual Variable models. A quantitative methodology was employed to gather and analyze respondent data from 150 farmers and agricultural extension workers in Lampung province. The data was processed using SmartPLS 4.0. This study established 12 hypotheses, of which 7 were confirmed and 5 were refuted, Average T-Statistics of accepted hypotheses: 2.318, Average P Values of accepted hypotheses: 0.016. The accepted hypothesis indicates a significant relationship between the variables This study emphasizes the significance of taking into account social dynamics and trust when promoting the adoption of IoT-based agricultural technologies. It offers valuable insights for policy makers and practitioners to develop successful strategies and policies that stimulate the adoption and utilization of these technologies.

articleTitle: OCTm: Custom Deep Learning Model for Diagnosing Retinal Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The retina is one of the most essential parts of the vision process and may be exposed to many diseases that require early diagnosis. In this paper, we applied several pre-processing steps and proposed a custom convolutional neural network (CNN) model called (OCTm), which consists of many layers and includes both types of convolutional layers (2-D convolutional and separable convolutional) and both types of pooling layers (max and average). Has been implemented for diagnosing retinal diseases, namely Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV), Diabetic Macular Edema (DME), and DRUSEN, in optical coherence tomography (OCT) images in the UCSD-v2 dataset. It showed a high accuracy and speed that was able to obtain an accuracy of up to 99.79%, 100% specificity, 99.79% precision, and 99.69% sensitivity. When comparing the accuracy of the proposed model, it exceeds the results of previous studies. The Duke dataset was also used to verify the generalizability of the model and achieved an accuracy of 99.69%, a specificity of 100%, a precision of 99.69%, and a sensitivity of 99.69%. These results confirm the reliability of the use of artificial intelligence in the medical field.

articleTitle: Modified Positive Output Super Lift Luo Converter Based on Switched Capacitor Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This paper presents the improved design of the Luo converter (POSLLC) by removing one diode and adding a switched capacitor (SC) cell at the output simulated in MATLAB/Simulink. The SC cell improves the dependability and lifespan of the source and maintains the input voltage. The SC cell provides More voltage amplification, particularly for high-gain purposes. Utilizing a single power switch, the suggested converter streamlines control procedures while dramatically increasing input voltage by 21 times with a duty cycle of (0.9). This outperforms the benefits made by Luo converters by 11 times and by ordinary boost converters by more than 10 times. The simplicity of the suggested converter stems from the fact that it only uses a single power switch, three capacitors and three diodes. To validate the theoretical underpinnings of the research, the study included comprehensive mathematical analysis and simulations.

articleTitle: Wavelet Entropy and Support Vector Machine Multi-Class Fall Detection Based on IMU Wearable Sensors Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Fall detection is especially important for seniors because falls are one of the main health dangers for the elderly in public health care. Elderly people are particularly vulnerable to falls, which can result in serious injuries, especially if the person who falls remains on the ground for an extended period without help. In this paper, we proposed a fall detection system-based Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensor to improve the detection method. Wavelet entropy for feature extraction and a directed acyclic graph support vector machine (DAG-SVM) classifier for multi-class classification are then applied. The proposed system is evaluated on a ready-made dataset based on multi-wearable sensors; data come from multi-sensors chest, thigh, and waist IMU datasets. The multi-class classification approach splits the elderly activities into three phases: pre-fall, impact, and post-fall. Experimental results, relying on using a single accuracy in fall detection were compared with multiple sensors and achieved 71.66%, 71.64%, and 97.79%, with different sensor locations. The results showed that the proposed model-based multi-wearable sensors demonstrated high accuracy compared to the model-based single sensor.

articleTitle: Comparing Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) for Auto-Cooling System in Generator Rotor Straightening
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: During the process of straightening the generator rotor using thermo-mechanical method, it’s crucial to have a thermal barrier or cooling system to prevent heat from spreading to other areas. Excessive heat can damage the generator winding or even cause a fire. Therefore, it’s important to have a well-controlled cooling system in place to ensure the final product’s quality. One way to do this is to use advanced algorithms of automatic control systems such as FLC and ANFIS. This study utilizes a simulation-based methodology to assess and compare the efficiency of FLC and ANFIS algorithms in MATLAB. Following the simulation, the results are compared to those obtained from the SolidWorks application, which utilizes Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). Based on the test results, it was found that the Thermo-Mechanical Straightening Method is more effective when using ANFIS than FLC for automatic cooling. The MAD value for FLC was 7.06, with a MAPE value of 288.33, and an MSE value of 54.14, resulting in an RMSE value of 7.35. On the other hand, ANFIS produced a MAD value of 0.14, a MAPE value of 3.96, and an MSE of 0.03, with an RMSE value of 0.18. These results indicate that ANFIS is a more efficient method for automatic cooling based on the Thermo-Mechanical Straightening Method.

articleTitle: Determining The Parameter K of K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) using Random Grid Search
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The study aims to optimize the classification of reception of training participants using the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm by finding the optimal value for the K parameter through a combination of search methods, Random search and grid search. This approach is expected to address the problem of manuality in the selection process of training participants who are susceptible to human error. The grid search method is used to search for parameter values in sequence, while the random search methods are used for optimum value search efficiency. The results showed that random grid search obtained accuracy of 91% with K=5, using manhattan metric, and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.081. These findings contribute to improving the efficiency and accuracy of the classification process by automatically accepting training participants using machine learning approaches, with results relevant to the development of similar systems in the future.

articleTitle: Optimizing Rice Variety Recognition Through Transfer Learning with Pretrained ResNet Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The identification of rice varieties holds paramount importance in addressing global food challenges, given that rice serves as a staple food source for more than half of the world’s population. Accurate identification is crucial for ensuring food security and meeting the dietary needs of diverse populations. However, accurately distinguishing between rice varieties remains a complex task due to genetic mixing and hybridization, which can lead to variations in morphological and genetic traits among different varieties. Recent advancements in deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), offer promising solutions for improving rice variety classification by leveraging large datasets and sophisticated image processing techniques. This study conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis of ResNet50 and ResNet101 models in identifying rice varieties using transfer learning and fine-tuning approaches. Leveraging a dataset containing 75,000 high-resolution rice images representing various varieties, the models undergo thorough evaluation based on various performance metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Results highlight the effectiveness of pretrained ResNet models in accurately classifying rice varieties, with ResNet50 achieving the highest accuracy of 98.813% post-fine-tuning. These findings underscore the significance of fine-tuning pretrained models to enhance classification accuracy, contributing to the advancement of precision agriculture and sustainable food production practices. The insights gained from this study have implications for improving crop management practices, optimizing resource allocation, and ultimately, enhancing global food security.

articleTitle: State of Charge Estimation of Lithium Ion Battery Using Coulomb Counting Method Based on Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This paper proposes a system which measures a single cell Lithium Ion Battery (LiB) nominal capacity using constant current discharge and constant current charge circuit, then Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) parameter extraction from Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC) test, then applying Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to estimate State of Charge (SOC) based on Raspberry Pi. In this process, the battery is prepared before the test using constant current constant voltage (CCCV) method. Then the battery undergoes nominal capacity identification. The nominal capacity identification is then used as standard for the time duration for HPPC pulse. After HPPC test is conducted, the second order Thevenin ECM parameters are extracted. The parameters are then fitted with the Coulomb Counting (Ah) method using the seventh order polynomial. The polynomial equation is then filtered using UKF method to estimate SOC. The SOC estimation result between the UKF and Ah is then compared. From the result, the UKF shows an ability to adjust to the reference value when given wrong initial SOC estimation. The root-mean square error (RMSE) and maximum error (ME) during the real-time experiment for UKF SOC is 27.6% and 9.99% respectively.

articleTitle: Determination the Quality of plain X-Ray Using Fuzzy Logic in View of Voltage, Current and Exposure Time Based on Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: In fulfilling the appropriate standard requirements, it is necessary to carry out a suitability test on the plain X-Ray to determine the deviation value of the tube voltage (kV), current (mA) and radiation time (sec) so that the radiation output value is still within the tolerance limits.. The method used is to measure the tube output voltage and the test results are then analyzed using the linear regression method using Python, so that the performance of the tool is obtained according to the established standards. From the results obtained, the % error value tested is a value below e-Max 10%, namely the average % error kVp 0.6%, mA 0.38% and $\mathrm{t} 2.06 \%$ then the performance value of the have plain X-Ray error (CL) 0.057 in the sense that $\mathrm{CL} \leqslant 0$ means where the radiation output value is still within tolerance and safe for the patient.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of KNN and C.45 Algorithms With Kappa Measure Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This study aims to develop an effective predictive model for forecasting students’ graduation status at the Health Polytechnic of the Ministry of Health in Medan. Using the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) method and the C4.5 algorithm, along with applying the SMOTE technique, addresses class imbalance in the dataset and enhances the accuracy of predicting students’ graduation. Data were obtained from the Health Polytechnic of the Ministry of Health in Medan, including lists of students who graduated and those who did not from 2018 to 2021. The dataset comprises 3997 records with 15 features, including student ID numbers, activity statuses, Grade Point Averages (GPAs), credit unit counts, and graduation statuses. Class imbalance handling was performed using SMOTE. The KNN and C4.5 models were evaluated with three K values (1,3, and 5) and three optimal node splitting methods. Model evaluation using the Kappa Measure indicated a high level of agreement between predicted and actual outcomes. Data normalization enhanced the consistency of analysis results, while SMOTE improved the quality of analysis and classification outcomes. Both the KNN and C4.5 models effectively predicted graduation statuses, with KNN showing improved performance with increasing K values. Cohen’s Kappa values confirmed high agreement across all models. The study’s conclusion underscores the effectiveness of data normalization, SMOTE, and predictive models (KNN and C4.5) in forecasting students’ graduation statuses, offering valuable insights to support decision-making in higher education institutions.

articleTitle: Regression Modeling for House Price Prediction in Java Island
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Houses have become significant commodity for many parties. For developers and buyers, houses prices are crucial considerations for property investment. Typically, house price predictions are made by experts. Automating predictions would ease various parties, including the government, in controlling price stability. House price predictions are extensively researched in various countries Like in China, Australia, Taiwan, Pakistan, India, Canada, Indonesia, and others. Generally, features for price prediction revolve around the size and furniture of the house without considering its location. House price in larger cities tend to be more expensive. Given this situation, this research focuses on the impact of city and province attribute on house price prediction. This research proposes to build a predictive model based on home size, furniture, and location. The model is built using several machine learning algorithms for regression measured by Mean Squared Error (MSE) metrics. Testing results show that predictions tend to improve when using location attributes for almost all algorithms. Additionally, simulations are conducted using other feature engineering and categorical encoding, increasing the MSE value of Random Forest up to $\mathbf{0. 0 0 0 6 8 1}$.

articleTitle: Improve the Quad copter Stability by Using An Adaptive Fuzzy Inference Neural Network (AFINN)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This work present adaptive fuzzy inference neural network (AFINN) controller for control of a quad copter system. The proposed controller uses least-mean square (LMS) algorithm to estimate an optimal flight of an unmanned quad copter. The simulation of control system performed by using Matlab/Simulink toolbox 2021b for thrust and attitude controlling by dynamic modeling of quad copter in Simulink and applied proportional-derivative (PD) controller to the plant, finally design AFINN controller and applied to the plant, the results of simulation for each controller was present and compared with each other. The outcomes of this work demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller that achieving minimum errors.

articleTitle: Leveraging IndoBert for CyberBullying Classification on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Cyberbullying is becoming an increasingly concerning issue, with a significant increase in cases every day. These incidents have profound negative impacts on victims, including emotional stress, mental health problems, and social withdrawal. This research aims to comprehensively examine the development and prevalence of cyberbullying cases in Indonesia. By utilizing sentiment analysis on Instagram comments, this study evaluates the accuracy and effectiveness of two prominent algorithms: Neural Network and IndoBERT (Indonesian Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers). The research findings indicate that the IndoBERT algorithm demonstrates superior performance, achieving high accuracy in identifying instances of cyberbullying. Specifically, IndoBERT shows an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$, precision of $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$, recall of $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$, and an F1 score of $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$. These results underscore the potential of advanced machine learning models in enhancing the detection of harmful online behavior. The study also recommends that future research should utilize larger datasets to further improve the accuracy and reliability of analysis.

articleTitle: Smart Stick Detecting Obstacles Early Using Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: In everyday life, blind people always have to face more difficulty. In modern technology, we can design convenient devices to help them live more easily. This paper focuses on designing a product for them. Specifically, a smart cane will be designed to help blind people avoid objects. To identify and classify objects, we use the random forest algorithm. Our main contribution is to build a detection system and classify obstacles early using cheap sensors and cameras. The results show that the model achieves an accuracy of up to $\mathbf{9 7. 8 7 \%}$ at a distance of up to 94 cm. The results show that the device is promised feasibility when applied in practice.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Apriori Algorithm with Transaction Reduction and Hash Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The apriori algorithm is an algorithm that generates candidate itemsets incrementally and recursively to calculate and combine itemsets until no candidate itemset. Apriori algorithm has limitations, namely requiring a lot of time to scan the database to calculate support and confidence. In this study, the performance improvement is the execution time parameter for data scanning, and then researchers propose a method to speed up the performance of the apriori algorithm by combining the transaction reduction and hash-based methods, where the transaction reduction method is expected to be able to reduce the data to be scanned in the database by eliminating data whose value is below the minimum support. Then the hashbased method is able to reduce the data to be scanned in the database because the data scanned is only the hash code, while the large itemsets data will be represented by the hash code without making the performance of the validity of the rules formed does not decrease. Because the most useful information from finding patterns using the apriori algorithm is the rules formed. So the time required to execute a large database can be reduced a lot with association rules that run according to the procedure. From the results of tests conducted by researchers, at 2-itemsets in the second iteration the processing time is reduced about 20 times faster, then in the 3-itemsets in the third iteration the processing time was reduced by around 790 times faster compared to the apriori algorithm without transaction reduction and hash based methods.

articleTitle: A Deep Feature Extraction for Hate Speech Detection using Fine-Tuned Naive Bayes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Hate speech on social media platforms like Twitter is a significant problem that can negatively affect individuals and communities, disrupting a healthy online environment. To address this problem, our study introduces a new method for detecting hate speech in Bahasa, combining Deep Feature Extraction (DFE) with a Fine-tuned Naive Bayes (FTNB) approach. This method uses an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to learn and extract complex patterns and semantic relationships from the text. These extracted features are then processed using a FTNB model to enhance decision-making. Integrating deep learning for feature extraction with the probabilistic approach of Naive Bayes (NB) significantly improves the model’s accuracy and precision in identifying hate speech.

articleTitle: Detection of Image Splicing and Copy-Move Forgery Using the Prewitt Operator and CNN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The ubiquity of digital images in our daily lives has a profound impact across various critical sectors. The advancement of image editing tools to a sophisticated level, coupled with their user-friendly interface, enables effortless image manipulation for users of all skill levels. Social media platforms have emerged as widely used channels for sharing content. Inappropriate images shared on these platforms can lead to legal consequences. Image manipulation techniques such as copy-move or splicing are standard practices. Deep learning leverages neural networks with multiple layers for independent processing, enabling the extraction of intricate features from data, which is particularly beneficial for tasks like image analysis. Convolutional neural network (CNN), renowned for its accuracy in image classification, consists of distinct layers, including convolutional layers, pooling layers, and fully connected layers. The Datasets utilized in this study comprise CASIA V2 and CoMoFoD. The validation accuracy results of our CNN model before integrating Prewitt were 81.05% for CASIA V2, 82.19% for CoMoFoD, and 80.43% for CASFoD. After adding Prewitt, the CNN model showed improved detection accuracy, reaching validation rates of 83.10% for CASIA V2, 86.30% for CoMoFod, and $\mathbf{8 2. 4 0 \%}$ for CASFoD.

articleTitle: Analysis of Three-Phase Grid Synchronization Algorithms Performance Under Harmonic Pollution to Grid Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The goal of this research is to assess the effectiveness of three-phase PLL algorithms when exposed to harmonic pollution in the grid voltage. Grid synchronization is a crucial aspect that needs to be done to overcome imperfections in a grid to ensure that the electricity has an optimal power quality and the operations remain efficient and seamless. Three PLL algorithms such as SRF-PLL, DSOGI-PLL, and DDSRFPLL are evaluated by involving third-order harmonics injection in the grid voltage. The results analysis will provide an understanding of the responses of each PLL algorithm in overcoming distorted grid voltage conditions. The results from simulations conducted with Matlab/Simulink are used to support the analysis that is provided. Based on the simulation results, DSOGI-PLL has the best output performance by estimating accurate phase angles and minimum oscillations under distorted grid voltage conditions.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of ChatGPT on Enhancing Academic Skills and Learning Concepts Among University Students in Jakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: There has been a noticeable change in the way that academic skill development and learning work with the introduction of ChatGPT as a key educational technology tool, especially for Jakarta university students. This study aims to clarify how ChatGPT helps students get a deeper knowledge and improve their academic performance, as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more and more integrated into educational environments. With a quantitative approach, we investigated the usefulness, interaction, flexibility, and possible drawbacks of ChatGPT in educational contexts using questionnaires. The results of 331 university students who participated in a snowball sampling process indicated a strong preference for ChatGPT as a tool to improve studying. The model is effective at enhancing learning experiences, according to preliminary results, but it also raises questions about the critical thinking abilities that may be compromised by an overreliance on artificial intelligence. Therefore, this study contributes and give insights into the application of ChatGPT in education, offering educational institutions, teacher, or student a comprehensive strategy for leveraging AI technology to improve the academic skill and learning concepts.

articleTitle: Fungi Image Segmentation using Efficient U-Net Architecture with ImageNet Pre-trained Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning techniques have shown remarkable performance in image segmentation tasks. Deep learning with a pre-trained model has been widely used to address the limited training data problem in microscopy image analysis. This research combined EfficientNet architecture with pre-trained ImageNet and U-Net architecture for fungi microscopic image segmentation tasks. The experiment result shows that the combination reached the best result, achieving an IoU of 0.818 and an F1-score of 0.899.

articleTitle: Examining Reliability in Delay Tolerant Networks: A Study of Protocol Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Delay Tolerant Networks (DTN) are crucial in ensuring communication resilience during emergencies, where conventional infrastructure may fail. This research investigates the reliability and performance of various DTN routing protocols under different scenarios, including Epidemic, Spray-and-Wait, MaxProp, First Contact, and Direct Delivery. Critical parameters such as delivery probability, overhead ratio, average latency, and average buffer time are evaluated to understand protocol behavior. Using simulations conducted at Telkom University, this study provides insights into protocol effectiveness in scenarios of node growth and buffer size increase. The results highlight the Spray-and-Wait protocol’s superior reliability in node growth scenarios and its effectiveness in maintaining performance during buffer size increases. Additionally, research findings on the performance of each protocol are summarized, providing a comprehensive overview of their strengths and weaknesses. This research advances emergency communication infrastructure by providing valuable insights for protocol optimization and system resilience enhancement.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Using K-NN Algorithm Through Random Search Cross Validation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This research discusses the application of the KNearest Neighbor (K-NN) algorithm in sentiment analysis, specifically in classifying positive, negative, or neutral sentiments from ChatGPT user opinions collected from user reviews on the Play Store. This research focuses on optimizing the key parameters of the K-NN algorithm using the Random Search cross-validation (RSCV) method. The evaluation results showed a good performance improvement after applying RSCV. Previously, the model showed unsatisfactory performance but improved significantly after optimization. Overall, RSCV successfully improved the average performance of the model for sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Indonesian Dynamic Sign Language Recognition for Individuals with Sensory Disabilities using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: People with disabilities often face difficulties communicating with the general public, especially regarding sign language. Sign Language Recognition (SLR) is a technology focused on recognizing, interpreting, and translating sign language into text or speech. SLRs can be divided into two types: static and dynamic. This research focuses on dynamic sign language recognition to develop recognition for Indonesian Sign Language, using the Python programming language with libraries such as Mediapipe, cvzone, sklearn, numpy, and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) technique. These findings show the potential of SLR technology in assisting communication for individuals with disabilities in Indonesia. This research significantly contributes to the development of Indonesian Sign Language SLR.

articleTitle: Implementation of the EfficientNet Model for Identification of Wild Edible Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Wild plants are plants that are not cultivated but wild plants can be easily found in the neighborhood. However, not all wild plants can be utilized as food crops by the community. Therefore, it is necessary to know what wild plants can be consumed so that people do not have to worry about food availability. The purpose of this study is to determine whether the EfficientNet model can be used to identify wild plants that can be consumed. Experimental results show that the EfficientNet model has an accuracy of 85% in identifying wild plants that can be consumed.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking Using Differential Evolution Algorithm on the SEPIC Converter for Solar Panels Under Partially Shaded Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) systems often encounter issues stemming from partial shading, which not only diminishes system output power but also compromises safety and operational efficiency. Employing Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) with utmost efficiency enables PV systems to consistently achieve peak power production. To address shading-induced challenges, a differential evolution algorithm is utilized within the Maximum Power Point (MPP) tracking algorithm, allowing for effective tracking of the global MPP even amidst partial shading scenarios. In this study, a Single-Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC) converter integrated with an MPPT system is employed to optimize power extraction from PV panels, particularly under conditions characterized by multiple peaks in both the $P-V$ and I-V curves. The proposed algorithm demonstrates the capability to track the global MPP within a timeframe of 0.8 seconds.

articleTitle: Construction of a Self-Balancing Cube With Embedded Reaction Wheel Drive and Preliminary Investigation of Simple Harmonic Motion Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The use of reaction wheels to help maintain the position of objects in balance remains an interesting topic to discuss in research. The harmonic motion resulting from the continuous rotation of the reaction wheel is read by the installed sensor, so that acceleration and angular velocity values are obtained on the X -axis, Y -axis and Z -axis. The self-balancing cube was built to be used as a vehicle for the reaction wheel to be embedded. The phenomenon that occurred during the experiment showed that there was a certain pattern formed as a result of the self-balancing cube swinging to maintain its balance.

articleTitle: Designing of System for Monitoring and Forecasting Air Environment Using LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: In the modern era, the problem of air pollution is becoming increasingly serious, affecting public health and causing significant environmental damage. Building and designing an air monitoring station system is important in effectively monitoring and evaluating air quality to face this challenge. At the same time, using data from this system to predict future trends and fluctuations is important for developing and improving air quality. The paper focuses on creating a modern monitoring system and predicts future air conditions using the long short-term memory (LSTM) model. We have combined advanced technologies and predictive models to provide accurate and complete information about air quality.

articleTitle: Object Detection in Low-Light Conditions: A Comparison using YOLOv5 and YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Object detection refers to identifying objects by determining their presence, location, and size, and assigning appropriate class labels. Detecting objects under low-light conditions presents challenges due to insufficient illumination, leading to decreased object visibility. In previous experiments, YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 were used to detect objects. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 models in detecting objects in low-light scenarios. The datasets used in this research contain 4,132 low-light images obtained from the publicly available Roboflow dataset. Evaluating the performance of YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 models involves using metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and mAP values. Based on a comparison performance, YOLOv8 outperforms YOLOv5. The results of precision, recall, F1-Score, and mAP values indicate that the YOLOv8 model performance exceeds the YOLOv5 model, with differences of 6.14%, 10.61%, 9%, and 11.89%, respectively, for each performance metric.

articleTitle: Texture Analysis of Scalogram Image from Alcoholic EEG Signals using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The harmful use of alcohol has become a significant global health issue, causing millions of deaths annually and contributing to various diseases and mental disorders. Early diagnosis of alcoholism is crucial to prevent permanent damage, yet current diagnostic methods are subjective and prone to errors. his study proposes an objective approach using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for identifying alcoholism. We employ Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) for signal preprocessing and Grey-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) for feature extraction, followed by classification with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The results show a classification accuracy of 99% in distinguishing alcoholic and non-alcoholic individuals based on EEG signals. This research contributes to the development of alcoholic diagnosis and highlights the potential of EEG technology with the combined use of CWT, GLCM, and CNN techniques to enhance accuracy in alcoholic identification.

articleTitle: Design Improved Transimpedance CMOS amplifier for optical Receiver front end
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: A complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) with TIA is one of the essential components for the performance of an optical receiver. It has a significant impact on the performance of optical receivers. Advances in this technology provide noise reduction and increased data transfer rate by converting optical signals into electrical signals. This article examines the design process of a low-noise CMOS amplifier with receive interface TIA technology, to achieve high-quality signals in applications such as optical receiver performance. It is necessary to reduce noise interference and obtain accurate analog signals from the current entering the carrier. I demonstrated the process of this design with up to 30 Gbit/s CMOS for the front end of a low-power optical transceiver. It has been shown that single-ended and differential photo inverters based on float-body transistors can achieve an oscillating voltage of 4 VPP volts per point. At 30 GHz up, the individual gain is measured and this defines the impedance amplifier (TIA). The device parameters derived from the proposed design method closely match the simulated results generated using LTspice.

articleTitle: Reduction of Microarray Data Dimensions to Enhance Performance of Naïve Bayes in Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: According to data Global Burden of Cancer Survey (Globocan) by World Health Organization (WHO) in 2018 there were 18.1 million new cases with a death rate of 9.6 million deaths, where 1 in 8 men and 1 in 11 women died of cancer. The death rate could be prevented with a comprehensive management system that starts with early detection, prevention, and treatment [2]. In the study of microarray data for cancer early detection, the properties of high-dimensional data, small sample sizes, and noise, must be treated seriously because they can affect the classifier’s performance. This is critical for dealing with the curse of dimensionality and the inability to identify important information hidden in microarray data. Therefore, we propose PCA method for dimensionality reduction of microarray data to support Naive Bayes algorithm to complish classification tasks. Based on the studies we conducted, we discovered an increases of performance classification where the accuracy achieved is $\mathbf{9 2. 1 1 \%}$, precision $\mathbf{9 0. 2 0 \%}$ and the $\mathbf{f 1}$-score is $\mathbf{9 3. 8 8 \%}$ for ovarian cancer and prostate cancer had the accuracy is 93.55%, precision and $\mathbf{f 1 -}$ score reached $\mathbf{9 2. 8 6 \%}$.

articleTitle: Implementation of Distributed Wide Area Monitoring System Server Configuration on Java-Madura-Bali Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: PLN, as the Indonesian electricity company, has implemented large-scale monitoring systems. One of these monitoring systems is Wide Area Monitoring Systems (WAMS), which aims to monitor any measurements in the Java-Madura-Bali (Jamali) power system. The WAMS server in the control center and the phasor measurement unit (PMU) in the substation connect to each other. The centralized WAMS server has two functions: phasor data concentrator (PDC) and historian. Initially, the WAMS on the Java-Madura-Bali system could monitor as many as 38 PMUs from various locations, with a CPU utilization of 57%, and the WAMS server could operate normally. When 32 PMUs were added, problems arose because the CPU utilization on the WAMS server reached 100%. This happens because one server does all the processing for the PDC, historian, and vector processor, so all data in WAMS is lost. The test results show that the historian requires more CPU and memory resources when compared to the PDC. Thus, the PDC and historian applications need to be separated on different servers. Based on previous research related to distributed real-time servers, this paper provides a short-term solution in the form of separating PDC and historian servers and a long-term solution for the Java-Madura-Bali WAMS configuration. The short-term solution results in the performance status on the historian server being at 8%, so WAMS is in a safe condition. The long-term solution is in the form of a regionalization system where PDC servers are located in each area or region. This solution can be used as a reference for other power systems that will implement WAMS.

articleTitle: Pipeline Leak Classification using Machine Learning Ensemble Methods and Hyperparameter Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This study focuses on developing and evaluating machine learning models to classify five distinct types of leaks in water distribution systems: Circumferential Crack, Gasket Leak, Longitudinal Crack, No Leak, and Orifice Leak. Its objective is to enhance classification accuracy using the bagging ensemble method and hyperparameter tuning using random search. The dataset comprises “.raw” format audio signals captured via hydrophone sensors, converted to ‘.wav’ format, and segmented into 2-second clips. Pre-processing involves extracting acoustic features like Spectral Centroid, Spectral Bandwidth, Spectral Rolloff, Spectral Flatness, and Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). Four machine learning models—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)—are employed for classification. Model evaluation employs k-fold cross-validation, assessing accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and support metrics. These models achieve accuracy scores, with ANN leading at 92%, closely followed by LSTM at 91%, SVM at 90%, and Random Forest at 86%.

articleTitle: Skin Melanoma diagnosis using machine learning and ABCD rule
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Skin cancer, being the most predominant type of malignant growth, represents more than half of all cancer instances. While melanoma is less common than other skin cancers, it poses the highest risk due to its tendency to metastasize and potentially result in mortality. Nonetheless, early detection significantly increases the chances of curing melanoma. The detection of melanoma poses a considerable challenge, primarily attributed to the minimal interclass variance observed between images of melanoma and non-melanoma, alongside the heightened interclass variance within melanoma images. Hence, it is imperative to formulate a Computer-aided Diagnosis (CAD) to identify such lesions and facilitate early disease diagnosis to enhance the probability of patient survival. The proposed methodology consists of a sequence of four distinct phases. The initial stage involves preprocessing, which incorporates the application of filtering and contrast enhancement algorithms such as the Median filter, Dull razor, and Histogram Equalization. The segmentation process proceeds by utilizing Otsu methods in order to detect any anomalies. Subsequently, the following phase involves the extraction of features through GLCM for textural attributes and ABCD base parameters, encompassing asymmetry, border irregularity, color, and diameter. Following this, a model based on artificial neural networks (ANN) is developed by leveraging these extracted traits to discern instances of skin cancer within the provided dataset. This methodology achieves a commendable overall accuracy rate of 99%. Dermatologists may derive significant assistance in their clinical decision-making procedures from this promising breakthrough.

articleTitle: Active Gate Driver with RC Snubber and Proportional-Integral (PI) Controller for Voltage Balancing of Series Connected SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The series connection of silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs and cascaded systems allows operating at higher voltages than those specified of devices. However, there is an issue of unbalanced drain-source voltages occurring in the devices connected in series. The primary reason for this imbalance is the parasitic capacitance in SiC MOSFETs. Several methods exist for balancing the voltages of series-connected devices, such as snubber circuits and active gate controllers. In this paper, we propose the utilization of an RC snubber and an active gate driver, specifically a proportional-integral (PI) controller with PWM feedback, to reduce the unbalanced drain-source voltages in the devices. Finally, we validate RC snubber and active gate driver for series connection SiC MOSFET through simulation using LTSpice XVII.

articleTitle: An Efficient Hybrid Model for Federated Learning Systems to Deal with Medical Heterogeneous Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a popular topic for developing Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications. This technology trains its models using data from many clients working together without sharing their data. Data privacy is protected by local training. Because this technology is new, researchers had difficulty dealing with heterogeneous data across clients. Non-identical, independent (non-IID) distribution and data type changes across clients may affect the global model predictions. This study examined how to handle clients with diverse data in quantity and kind. Datasets have been collected on people infected and not infected with the Coronavirus. Two different types of datasets, X-rays, and CT scans were selected and these datasets have been distributed unevenly among four clients participating in the system. A hybrid model has been built consisting of convolutional neural networks and long short-term memory (CNN&LSTM) to train this dataset and predict the diagnosis of this disease. Excellent result was obtained in all clients, reaching 99% in one of these clients.

articleTitle: Forensic Investigation of User Privacy Violation by Android Malware with Hybrid Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Technology-based fraud, which sends Android Package Kit (.apk) files to smartphone users, is often used to steal data by inserting malware into the applications sent. To overcome this, reverse engineering is needed on files suspected of containing malware. So that an analysis of the application program code infected with malware can be performed. This research proposes static and dynamic analysis methods to monitor malware activity which is violating smartphone users’ privacy. This research uses two types of malwares that are popular in Indonesia, namely, wedding-invitation.apk and airwaybill.apk. The experiment shows that the reverse engineering can help us understand the malware behavior.

articleTitle: Exploration of Internal Factors Influencing the Success of Digital Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Despite the digital projects are increasingly emerging as forms of digital transformation, there are still many failures in conducting digital projects. This study aims to analyze the relationship between certain internal factors and the success of digital projects. Statistical analysis results indicate that the types of team members, whether full-time or part-time, and the experience level of team members do not have a significant relationship with project success. However, project ownership, adaptability, team leadership, method consistency, and the appropriateness of development methods significantly contribute to the success of digital projects. This study concludes that the success of digital projects can be achieved through a high sense of project ownership, adaptability, effective team leadership, method consistency, and the implementation of appropriate development methods. These factors can serve as essential guidelines in planning, managing, and evaluating digital projects to effectively achieve their goals.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Voltage Quality through DSTATCOM Implementation in the Electrical Infrastructure of Semen Tonasa
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Voltage quality problem, such as voltage drop, or voltage sag, is a common issue faced in electrical power systems, especially when dealing with large inductive loads. This challenge is encountered by one of the cement factories in Indonesia, often referred to as the largest cement factory in Eastern Indonesia. The electric motors used in cement production are significant contributors to reactive power in the electrical system of PT. Semen Tonasa, thereby exacerbating voltage drop issues. A system’s concern is when it fails to maintain voltage levels within acceptable limits, leading to further problems such as load shedding or even damage to electrical equipment. One of possible solution to address this issue, is the installation of D-STATCOM. Therefore, the research aims to analyze the application of D-STATCOM to improve voltage quality in Semen Tonasa electrical system using Particle Swarm Optimization method. Feasiblity analysis of DSTATCOM installation is also conducted in this research. The results indicate a positive impact on the voltage increase, which initially at 0.94 p.u., can be raised above 0.95 p.u., or by approximately $1 \%$.

articleTitle: Long Short-Term Memory Utilization for Non-Invertible Transformation Face Biometric Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: A recognition system is important in artificial intelligence research areas. It is broadly used for identification reasons and in several ways like facial recognition. Recognition systems depend on classification systems to work. Classification is a supervised learning technique. Long short-term memory is a type of supervised learning technique and can be used for classification purposes. Feature selection techniques have been used to improve the classification performance and reduce the training time. The black widow optimization algorithm is considered a kind of feature selection technique. Biometric systems are a particular type of recognition system. It influences the recognition system to accomplish its kernel work in identifying users based on the user’s unique biometric data. Face images are broadly used as a biometric trait. Facial recognition is popular, because of its non-intrusive, technological development, and cameras, nowadays, everywhere. Facial recognition is a common selection for detecting known users in secret zones. In this paper, the black widow optimization algorithm has been used to select the suitable feature. Then, the proposed non-invertible transformation method is performed to secure the selected feature. Finally, long short-term memory has been used as a classifier to classify known and unknown users. Two common datasets have been used to evaluate the proposed system. These datasets are FEI and Georgia Tech datasets. Two common measurements have been used to assess the proposed system. These measurements are the classification accuracy and the equal error rate. The experimental results show that the average classification accuracy was 98.61% for the FEI dataset and 98.21% for the Georgia Tech dataset. The average value for equal error rate was 0.68% for the FEI dataset and 0.86% for the Georgia Tech dataset.

articleTitle: Classification System of Breast Cancer using Machine Learning on Hu Moment Invariants and GLCM Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Breast cancer is a devastating disease with a high mortality rate. In most cases, women are the ones suffering from breast cancer. Mammogram screening is the most prevalent method to diagnose this disease. The mammogram images are manually examined by radiologists. Machine learning can help medical personnel and reduce the possibility of misdiagnosis. The Hu moment and Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) were employed for feature extraction. Moreover, Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) were utilized for breast cancer classification. The mammogram images in this study were taken from the Curated Breast Imaging Subset of Digital Database Screening Mammography (CBIS-DDSM). GLCM combined with Weighted KNN depicted the highest accuracy of 97.8%.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Discrete Wavelet Transformation Method with K-Nearest Neighbor in Eye Disease Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The eye is one of the senses in humans that functions as seeing objects by the reflecting light received by the retina. The eye has a vital role in carrying out daily activities, if the eye is attacked by diseases such as cataracts, it causes sufferers to experience disturbing vision, for example, a cataract eye disease that attacks the lens of the eye interferes with the retina in receiving light from outside. In a case Based on national data from the Rapid Assessment of Avoidable (RAAB) Blindness Survey in 2014 - 2016 by the Ministry of Health, cataracts are the highest cause of blindness with a presentation of 81% This type of eye disease known in this study are haven 3 cases, namely, cataracts, glaucoma, and retinal abnormalities. Then, in this case, a study was conducted that applied a system from machine learning to identify the type of disease through an image of the retinal fundus. The wavelet transformation method is created as image processing for decomposition and K- Nearest Neighbor as a learning method from machine learning. This study used data in the form of images with 4 different classes, among others, Normal with the number of images 300, cataracts with several images 100, glaucoma with the number of images 101, and retina diseases with the number of images 100. In total, there are 601 datasets obtained from the Kaggle website. Results of the application of this method in identifying sufficient performance with an accuracy rate of 61%.

articleTitle: Classification for Human Resource Talent Management Using Support Vector Machine Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Talent Management is a very important process for organizations to identify, manage, and retain talented individuals in order to achieve the company’s strategic goals. In the midst of increasingly fierce competition, companies are faced with the challenge of devising effective strategies to manage their human resources. However, the main drawback in the current system still lies in the use of recommendation systems that tend to be subjective, not based on the results of ability tests, employee performance, and psychological tests. One approach that has been applied is to use machine learning methods to overcome these weaknesses. This research aims to overcome the shortcomings in the structural position recommendation process by proposing an approach based on Support Vector Machine (SVM). In this study, we collected data from a university in A to develop a prediction model using the SVM method. The data used includes information on employees’ abilities, performance, and psychometric aspects. After an intensive training process, the SVM model we developed was tested and evaluated for its performance based on predefined criteria. The experimental results show that the SVM approach in talent management can deliver promising results. The resulting model is able to provide more objective and efficient job recommendations, and reduce the level of subjectivity that often arises in the recruitment and placement process. These findings highlight the great potential of machine learning methods in improving the effectiveness of talent management in various industrial sectors.

articleTitle: Implementation P-Wave Detection in a Seismic Waveform Using PhaseNet
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Indonesia is located in an active tectonic zone with a high frequency of earthquakes. One of the factors is due to Indonesia’s location, which is between the meeting of three tectonic plates: the Indo-Australian, Eurasian, and Pacific. The impact results in life loss, infrastructure damage, and other material losses. An earthquake monitoring instrument is essential to reduce these impacts. A seismometer and accelerometer are instruments that are used to monitor earthquakes. In processing wave data by seismic sensors, one is determining the arrival time of P-wave and S-wave from sensor recordings. P-wave is an essential parameter in the Earthquake Early Warning System stage. In the first second after the P wave is detected, the accelerometer can estimate earthquake parameters, assess the danger of earthquake motion, and be used as an alarm in real-time from accelerometer measurements. The picking process using traditional methods results in subjective interpretations and long processing times and tends to be inconsistent for extensive data. This study implemented PhaseNet based on deep learning for the detection of P-wave and S-wave in an earthquake event in the Bayah area on January 3, 2024. The result of this study shows that the phase score of the P -wave value in CSJI, CNJI, and PBJI is 0.858. 0.862 and 0.909, then S-wave values 0.634, 0.558, and 0.536. Model phase net has been successfully implemented using raw data signal accelerometer and is suitable for applying to areas with a specific scope and dynamic seismic.

articleTitle: Multilingual Named Entity Recognition Model for Location and Time Extraction of Forest Fire
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: The scarcity and limited access to multilingual datasets can hinder the training of named entity recognition models, especially for the application of social media sensing in disaster management, such as forest fires. Additionally, creating high-quality datasets also requires significant resources and efforts. Overcoming the limited availability of multilingual named entity recognition datasets in disaster management is a possible approach to reducing resources and efforts in order to make it more efficient. Therefore, this paper will compare the performance of several pre-trained multilingual BERT-based models on a web-based general-purpose dataset in Indonesian to extract the location and time of forest fires from social media text like Twitter. The fine-tuning results show that XLMRoBERTa (XLM-R) obtains the best performance with a validation loss of 0.0567, precision of 0.92, recall of 0.93, F1score of 0.92 and accuracy of 0.98. Testing results also show that XLM-R achieves the best overall performance on each label entity. The tweet validation results also obtained an acceptable accuracy of more than $50 \%$ for languages that were not in the main dataset.

articleTitle: Use of an Expert System to Diagnose and Provide Solutions for Pests and Diseases in Hydroponic Mustard Plants Using Certainty Factor and Forward Chaining Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Mustard greens are a vegetable that is very popular with people, especially hydroponic mustard greens, which appear fresher. However, like other vegetables, mustard greens grown hydroponically are also susceptible to pests and diseases, which can cause the vegetables to lose their freshness and may even result in crop failure. This condition can cause losses for mustard greens farmers in running their businesses. This research proposes an information system that represents the expertise of hydroponic mustard greens farmers in diagnosing pests and diseases in mustard plants as well as solutions to overcome them. This is to make it easier for novice growers and anyone interested in learning about diseases or pests that impact hydroponic mustard greens. The expert system developed is web-based and functions as a user consultation medium in relation to mustard pests and diseases using the forward chaining and certainy factor method to explain the decision tree procedure for mustard plant disease symptoms. With this expert system, farmers do not need to look for people who can explain the problems they face. We found that there were 10 types of pests and diseases and 29 symptoms in the hydroponic mustard plants reviewed in this research.

articleTitle: Pricing Strategies Using Design of Experiment in Online and Offline Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: This study examines pricing methods in both online and offline supply chains, which is a topic of increasing importance in current business conversations. The study focuses on examining the circumstances surrounding dual supply chains, in which producers employ both channels to cater to a wide range of customer demands. To assess the influence of pricing on the system’s dynamics, the study uses response surface methodology. The results uncover the most effective price levels for online and offline channels. Notably, the shift from online to offline channels shows a substantial rise in demand, but the opposite transfer leads to a rather moderate increase. These findings highlight the critical role of pricing strategies in enhancing profitability, particularly by prioritizing offline channels. The study provides significant insights for decision-makers who are dealing with the intricacies of contemporary supply chains, offering practical advice for optimizing business outcomes in this diverse setting.

articleTitle: Heart Rate Measuring System using Accelerometer And Gyroscope Sensor in Android Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Heart rate is an important indicator of human health, reflecting physiological conditions and cardiovascular problems. Research and development in the field of heart rate measurement continues to grow, utilizing accelerometer and gyroscope sensors as well as techniques such as R peak detection, digital bandpass, and peak detection. However, previous research was hampered by the smartphone API’s 100 Hz measurement frequency limit, so the sensitivity and accuracy of measurements were limited. This research aims to develop a measurement method for a more accurate heart rate using an Android smartphone with a measurement frequency of up to 200 Hz. The method used is Seismocardiography (SCG) with Aortic Open (AO) peak detection on accelerometer and gyroscope sensors. Heart rate data was collected from 20 healthy subjects using a Samsung A50 smartphone and Sensor Logger software and then processed using MATLAB R2015a to extract heart rate information. The SCG signal was processed with a bandpass filter and Hilbert transforms to obtain the envelope of the heart rate signal. The Aortic Open (AO) peak detection determines the heartbeat time. The SCG signal is processed with Baseline Wander Removal, Savitzky-Golay Filter, and Hilbert Transform to obtain the envelope of the heartbeat signal. The Aortic Open (AO) peak detection determines the heartbeat time estimation. The results showed that the SCG signal extraction method and Aortic Open (AO) peak detection achieved an accuracy of 99.3% for placement in the Upper abdomen and 97.36% for placement in the Sternum. This research provides a solution for more accurate and accessible heart rate measurement by utilizing existing smartphone technology.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection with Multi Layer Perceptron: Unveiling Neuron Unit Dynamics in Dual Hidden Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Breast cancer represents a significant global health burden, with millions of new cases diagnosed each year, making it the most common cancer in women worldwide and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Early detection is crucial for improving patient outcomes and reducing mortality rates associated with breast cancer. Machine learning techniques offer promising avenues for enhancing early detection and diagnosis. In this study, we investigate the performance of Multi Layer Perceptron (MLP) models with varying numbers of neuron units in two hidden layers for breast cancer diagnosis. Through systematic experimentation, we identify the optimal configuration, achieving the highest accuracy of 84.91% with the first hidden layer containing 5 neuron units and the second hidden layer containing 10 neuron units. Interestingly, competitive performance is observed in models with 5 neuron units in both hidden layers, showcasing accuracy levels ranging from 84.8% to 84.9%. Variations in other performance metrics across different configurations are minor. Overall, MLP models with 10 neuron units in both hidden layers demonstrate superior performance, with models featuring 5 units in both layers as viable alternatives. These findings underscore the versatility of MLP models in healthcare applications and contribute valuable insights to breast cancer diagnostics.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Film Bulk Acoustic wave Resonator with different piezoelectric materials
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Thin Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator (FBAR) is a device consisting of a piezoelectric material sandwiched between two electrodes and acoustically decoupled from the surrounding medium. The selection of piezoelectric materials is one of the most critical issues for the fabrication of high-performance FBAR devices. In this paper, two piezoelectric materials are used to design FBAR which is AIScN (aluminum scandium nitride) and AIN (aluminum nitride). The purpose of this demonstration was to compare the performance of the AIScN-based FBAR to the AIN-based FBAR, with both devices having identical geometries. AIScN and AIN are used in FBAR devices due to their excellent piezoelectric properties. However, AIScN has been gaining attention as a potential alternative to AIN due to its improved performance in certain aspects. Scandium (Sc) doping in the aluminum nitride lattice introduces strain, which enhances the piezoelectric properties of the material. This paper is the first one that demonstrated FBAR using $\mathrm{Al}_{0.88} \mathrm{Sc}_{0.12} \mathrm{~N}$ as a piezoelectric layer.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Equivalent Circuit Model Parameter Extraction Methods on Lithium-Ion Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference of Science and Information Technology in Smart Administration (ICSINTESA)
abstract: Lithium-Ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles due to their high efficiency and energy density. To produce accurate battery parameter measurements, a battery model that represents the characteristics of the battery is needed. The Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) uses an electrical circuit approach to model the battery. This paper evaluates the performance of four ECM parameter extraction methods obtained from four different references. The approach used in this method is curve fitting and constant time division during discharge and relaxation conditions in the battery. ECM parameter identification using Hybrid Pulse Power Characteristic (HPPC) test data during the discharge process. The performance of each method is evaluated by comparing simulated data against testing data. The RMSE values in method 1 when testing HPPC is 0.0104 V. Based on the comparison of RMSE values in each method, method 1 produces the most stable model when testing constant current profiles.

articleTitle: Extracting Gender Textual Nuances Using Text Similarity for Gender Classification Improvement
